chunks: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated from his father, from Ali ibn Sulayman ibn Rashid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Khazzaz, who said:

Ali ibn Abi Hamza came to Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) and asked him: 'Are you an Imam?' He said: 'Yes.' He said to him: 'I heard your grandfather Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) say: An Imam is not [one] unless he has an issue (offspring).' He said: 'Have you forgotten, O Shaykh, or did you misremember? This is not what Ja'far (peace be upon him) said. Rather, Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: An Imam is not [one] unless he has an issue, except for the Imam against whom al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him) rose up, for he has no issue.' He said to him: 'You have spoken the truth, may I be sacrificed for you. This is how I heard your grandfather say.'

key_terms.يَخْرُجُ عَلَيْهِ: Rises up against (referring to rebellion or uprising)

ai.seo_question: What is the exception to the rule that an Imam must have offspring according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the condition of having offspring ('aqib) for an Imam by distinguishing between the general rule established by Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq and a.s. and a specific exception regarding the Mahdi, identified here as the Imam against whom Husayn ibn Ali rose (often interpreted as Imam Hasan al-Askari or the Mahdi himself depending on the reading of 'yakhruju 'alayhi'). The dialogue highlights the scholarly transmission of this nuanced doctrine, affirming that while most Imams had offspring, the final Imam's lack of immediate, widely recognized offspring does not negate his Imamate, a key point in Shia eschatology regarding the Occultation.
